sentences.text: Einiosaurus was a medium-sized herbivorous dinosaur with an estimated body length of 4.5 meters, generally matching the size of Achelousaurus but possessing a much less robust build.
The specific name procurvicornis describes its unique nasal horn, which curved distinctly forward and downward.
Fossil evidence reveals six adult nasal horn cores, divided into two small, upright examples and four large ones that bent strongly toward the front.
The name Einiosaurus blends the Blackfoot word for buffalo with the Greek term for lizard.
Mass deaths occurred when these dinosaurs gathered around oxbow lakes during severe droughts, creating dense bone beds.
Jack Horner discovered remains of at least fifteen individuals of varying ages, including three adult skulls, in 1985.
Sampson formally named the genus and species Einiosaurus procurvicornis in 1994, basing the description on Horner's previously labeled Taxon B.
The holotype specimen, which serves as the primary example for the species, was unearthed in the Two Medicine Formation.
As a herbivore, Einiosaurus utilized a complex dental battery to process tough plant material efficiently.
A 2013 study determined that this dinosaur was restricted to feeding on vegetation standing one meter or lower in height.
Oxygen isotope analysis suggests Einiosaurus was a homeothermic endotherm, meaning it maintained a constant internal body temperature.
Research from 2010 concluded that the animal experienced rapid growth until its third to fifth year, a period likely coinciding with sexual maturity.
Single-species bone beds are interpreted as evidence of herding behavior, possibly resulting from catastrophic events like droughts or floods.
Einiosaurus is considered a herding animal with social behaviors similar to modern bison or wildebeest.
Einiosaurus is classified within the family Ceratopsidae, specifically belonging to the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
However, the placement of Einiosaurus within Centrosaurinae remains problematic due to the transitional nature of various skull characters.
This dinosaur lived between 83 and 74 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous Period.
Einiosaurus inhabited inland environments on a narrow coastal strip in Laramidia, bordered by the Western Interior Seaway and the 3 to 4 km high proto-Rocky Mountains.
The climate in which it lived was warm and semiarid.
Horner hypothesized that Einiosaurus represented a transitional form in an anagenetic lineage, arguing that the species evolved gradually without splitting into separate branches.

Some researchers, such as Dodson, argued against the anagenesis hypothesis, suggesting that the single pair of spikes in Einiosaurus indicated it was a separate branch rather than a direct descendant of Styracosaurus.
Later studies by Wilson and Scannella supported the idea that Achelousaurus was the direct descendant of Einiosaurus.
